findings.reason: the whole Deliverable (a new `set sections.<id>.<field>` path that creates the record, plus the §1 write-path surface in `reckon/_store_section_ops.py`) implements a capability the codebase already provides; the real, smaller defect is that the audit message advises the body-carrying append shape, so a node building this plan would duplicate a working mechanism and leave the actual message defect untouched.
findings.text:
the plan asserts "A legacy section therefore can never be given a record, and its audit error can never be cleared without hand-editing the plan's markup" and "Both write paths refuse that section", but only the *body-carrying* append and the `set` path refuse; the documented and supported body-less append already adopts the section. Measured against the main checkout's code (probe `probe.py`, log `probe-log.txt`: `module: /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/reckon/_store.py`) and `docs/plans/the-page-paints-from-an-index.html` §7: `apply_ops` with `{"op":"append","target":"sections","item":{"id":"s7","title":"…","effort_hours":2.0,"capability":{…},"links":[]}}` (no `body`) SUCCEEDS, and the subsequent `write_state` emits `

…

\n
` — the record element placed directly after the heading, which is precisely the placement the plan's Deliverable claims as new behaviour. The op vocabulary documents this route explicitly at `reckon/mcp.py:1752`: "target 'sections' … attaches a record to an `

` already in the file (item: id, no body)". The mechanism that performs the placement is `_splice_section_records` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1670-1683`), which finds the single matching h2 by identity and inserts the rendered record at its heading span's end, reached from `write_state` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:2240`). The plan's own measurement reproduced a refusal only because the audit message's worked example (`_section_contract_refusal`, `reckon/_store.py:1671-1689`) carries a `body`, which routes the item through `_insert_authored_section` and its `section id 's7' already exists` guard

findings.reason: the plan does not say how the audit's message alone is retargeted, so a node implementing it as written would either garble seven other refusals by editing the shared builder or need a write path the plan omits.
findings.text: the Deliverable requires "The audit's `section-without-contract` message names a write that succeeds on the section it reports: a `set` of each of `effort_hours` and `capability`", but that message is produced by `_section_contract_refusal` (`reckon/_store.py:1671`), a shared builder whose worked-example JSON is emitted by every caller — including `append sections requires an item object` (`reckon/_store.py:3035`) and `unsupported section fields` (`reckon/_store.py:1706`), where a `set` is not a remedy at all — and the `Finding` itself is constructed in `reckon/doccheck.py:1423`, which is not among the plan's declared write paths (`reckon/_store_section_ops.py`, `reckon/_store.py`, `tests/test_a_legacy_section_adopts_its_record.py`)

findings.reason: it is a soft relationship that steers no worker, and the same subject could arguably be carried by an open section-contract node instead.
